display.title: Episode 127: A Blessing from a Tzaddik, Chapter 1 (Erev Shavuos)
display.summary_short: The Erev Shavuos show: why everyone, even babies, should hear the Ten Commandments, the first chapter of a mysterious Baal Shem Tov story, and his yahrzeit on Shavuos.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Erev Shavuos 5744, with a new theme tune and the show's 127th week. Uncle Yossi reminds children that Mommy will light Yom Tov candles with a Shehecheyanu, and that everyone, from grandparents to babies in carriages, should be in shul tomorrow to hear the Aseres HaDibros, because the Torah was given in the merit of little children. After the Hakochainik march and a sponsor message, story time begins 'A Blessing from a Tzaddik'. Hashem gave Avraham the power to bless, and tzaddikim in every generation share it, but like rain on a field, a blessing only helps when the soil has been prepared by mitzvos. A traveler named Boruch struggles through a blinding snowstorm to an inn after midnight and finds an old man asleep by the fire. A five-year-old guest leads the Shema. Then a young man comes downstairs and harshly orders the old man up to serve the guest, and the old man hints that Boruch would never believe who the young man really is. To be continued. Uncle Yossi explains that this is a Baal Shem Tov story, told because his yahrzeit falls on Shavuos. A letter about Shmiras Halashon and Yom Tov wishes close the show.
display.lesson: Prepare yourself with mitzvos so a tzaddik's blessing can take root, and come to shul on Shavuos, children too, to hear the Ten Commandments.

date.note: 'Today is Erev Shavuos'; the Baal Shem Tov's passing in 1760 is '224 years ago'. Erev Shavuos 5744 was Tuesday 5 June 1984.
